newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia Chamber of Economy says wages too high.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia Chamber of Economy says wages too high.

text.p: The Slovenian Chamber of Economy business group said on Thursday that growth of salaries must be curbed urgently to avoid stifling the country's economy.

"We cannot allow wages to grow faster than production, because that could lead to increased unemployment and consequently seriously damage Slovenia's economy," Jozko Cuk, president of the Chamber told a news conference.
The average gross monthly salary in Slovenia, which reached 131,803 tolars ($970) in July, rose 14 percent in the first seven months of 1996 compared to the same period in 1995.
At the same time Slovenian industrial output fell 1.7 percent in the first seven months of 1996.
Earlier this month the Slovenian Association of Employers and the Chamber of Economy pushed for change to the collective agreement between employers and unions from the start of 1997.
They said the pact, which was inroduced in 1990 and renewed in 1993, should be amended in order to reduce benefits that financially troubled companies have to pay to employees.
Cuk said that high social benefits also deter potential foreign investors.
"If such a trend (of workforce costs) continues, foreign investors will avoid Slovenia, while local companies will begin searching for better investment conditions in other countries," Cuk added.
Direct foreign investment in Slovenia in 1995 rose to $176 million from $83.7 million a year earlier, representing just 0.8 percent of the country's GDP.
